datasets.name: 7dc06642
queryLines:
SELECT business_id, month, value
FROM (
  SELECT business_id,
         DATE_FORMAT(ADD_MONTHS(window_end, -k), 'yyyy-MM') AS month,
         churn_rate AS value
  FROM workspace.scribd_exercise.metrics_churn
  LATERAL VIEW EXPLODE(SEQUENCE(0, 2)) t AS k
  WHERE MONTH(window_end) IN (2, 5, 8, 11)
    AND billing_cycle = 'All billing cycles'
)
WHERE month >= '2023-01'

datasets.name: 1ef4350a
queryLines:
SELECT 'Active paid subscribers' AS metric,
       business_id,
       DATE_FORMAT(month_end, 'yyyy-MM') AS month,
       CONCAT('as of ', CAST(month_end AS STRING)) AS period,
       FORMAT_NUMBER(active_paid_subscribers, 0) AS headline,
       CONCAT('Up to ', FORMAT_NUMBER(upper_bound_paid_subscribers, 0)) AS range_or_ci
FROM workspace.scribd_exercise.metrics_active_subscribers
WHERE month_end >= DATE'2023-01-31'

UNION ALL

SELECT 'MRR' AS metric,
       business_id,
       DATE_FORMAT(month_end, 'yyyy-MM') AS month,
       CONCAT('as of ', CAST(month_end AS STRING)) AS period,
       CONCAT('$', FORMAT_NUMBER(mrr_usd, 2)) AS headline,
       CONCAT('Up to $', FORMAT_NUMBER(mrr_upper_bound_usd, 2)) AS range_or_ci
FROM workspace.scribd_exercise.metrics_mrr
WHERE month_end >= DATE'2023-01-31'

UNION ALL

SELECT metric, business_id, month, period, headline, range_or_ci
FROM (
  SELECT 'Churn rate (3 months)' AS metric,
         business_id,
         DATE_FORMAT(ADD_MONTHS(window_end, -k), 'yyyy-MM') AS month,
         CONCAT(DATE_FORMAT(window_start, 'MMM'), '–', DATE_FORMAT(window_end, 'MMM yyyy')) AS period,
         CONCAT(FORMAT_NUMBER(ROUND(CAST(churn_rate AS DECIMAL(10,4)) * 100, 1), 1), '%') AS headline,
         CONCAT('Likely between: ', FORMAT_NUMBER(ROUND(CAST(churn_rate_ci_low AS DECIMAL(10,4)) * 100, 1), 1), '% and ',
                FORMAT_NUMBER(ROUND(CAST(churn_rate_ci_high AS DECIMAL(10,4)) * 100, 1), 1), '%') AS range_or_ci
  FROM workspace.scribd_exercise.metrics_churn
  LATERAL VIEW EXPLODE(SEQUENCE(0, 2)) t AS k
  WHERE MONTH(window_end) IN (2, 5, 8, 11)
    AND billing_cycle = 'All billing cycles'
)
WHERE month >= '2023-01'

datasets.name: 1a47ccd3
queryLines:
SELECT sort_order,
       metric,
       CASE
         WHEN unit = 'USD per month' THEN CONCAT('$', FORMAT_NUMBER(raw_value, 2))
         WHEN unit IN ('users', 'people') THEN FORMAT_NUMBER(raw_value, 0)
         ELSE CONCAT(FORMAT_NUMBER(ROUND(CAST(raw_value AS DECIMAL(10,4)) * 100, 1), 1), '%')
       END AS raw,
       CASE
         WHEN unit = 'USD per month' THEN CONCAT('$', FORMAT_NUMBER(clean_value, 2))
         WHEN unit IN ('users', 'people') THEN FORMAT_NUMBER(clean_value, 0)
         ELSE CONCAT(FORMAT_NUMBER(ROUND(CAST(clean_value AS DECIMAL(10,4)) * 100, 1), 1), '%')
       END AS clean,
       pct_difference,
       impact_level,
       main_driver
FROM workspace.scribd_exercise.metrics_impact
ORDER BY sort_order

title.value: Which billing plan loses the most customers? (Churn rate by 3-month window)

description.value: Each point is a separate 3-month window (e.g., Jun-Aug 2026); windows don't overlap, so any two points can be compared. lines: **Data through August 2026.** Tables stop in mid-September, so later months would show false drops. Test accounts are removed. Placeholder prices are replaced with the plan's price from the price grid. Subscriptions with an unreliable status (test status, stale trials) are left out of the headline numbers but included in the upper end of each range. Churn is a 3-month rate, not monthly. See the Data trust page for how cleaning changed each number.

**Analysis findings (as of August 2026; full analysis in notebook 04)**

- Churn differs by billing cycle: monthly 27.2% vs. lifetime 4.8% over June–August (Fisher p < 0.001). This is an association, not evidence that lifetime deals cause retention.
- Churn does not differ reliably across businesses: BIZ\_1 15.7%, BIZ\_2 13.0%, BIZ\_3 11.1% (chi-square p = 0.66).
- Older content is much less likely to be reached: 66% vs. 97% for content under a year old (Fisher p < 0.001)

lines:
**How to read this page.**

- MAU = people who used the product in the month.
- Active paid subscribers = paying subscribers.
- MRR = monthly recurring revenue at listed prices.
- Churn = share of paying customers lost over 3 months.
- "Up to" numbers and shaded ranges show where the true value could be when some data is uncertain.

title.value: Month
How much of the activity goes to new vs. older content? (Engagement share vs. catalog share by content age

description.value: Share of content events (engagement) vs. share of live items (catalog) for each content age band. In August 2026, new content (0–90 days) was 7.7% of the catalog but got 29.2% of engagement; older content was 70% of the catalog and got 38%.

title.value: Which categories are seen least? (Catalog reach by category)

description.value: Share of live items in each category with at least one content event from a regular user in the month. Categories have 10–29 items each, so one item more or less moves a category's reach by several points. The thin lines show where the true value likely falls; when they overlap, the difference may be chance.

title.value: How complete is our catalog information? (Metadata Completeness)

description.value: Share of live items that pass each metadata requirement. "All requirements" is the share that passes every one. In August 2026, the only failing requirement is runtime: 10 items have placeholder runtimes (-1 or 99999).

title.value: Business
Is older content consistently seen less? (Catalog reach by content age over time)

description.value: Share of live items in each age band with at least one content event from a regular user in the month. All bands rise as active users grow, so focus on the gap between the lines: a persistent gap means older content is consistently less discovered. Starts in 2025; earlier months have too few new items for a stable rate. The shaded band shows where the true value likely falls; when they overlap, the difference may be chance.

lines:
**Analysis findings (as of August 2026; full analysis in notebook 04)**

- New content punches above its weight: content under 90 days old is 7.7% of the catalog but gets 29.2% of engagement (8.0 events per item vs. 1.2 for older content).
- Older content is much less likely to be discovered: 66% of older items were reached vs. 97% of items under a year old (Fisher p < 0.001), and older items make up 67 of the 70 items nobody engaged with.
- BIZ\_1's lower reach is largely a mix effect: its catalog is mostly older content (3.8% new vs. 15.8% for BIZ\_3). This is an association; the data can't separate category from business.
- Metadata is 96.5% complete; the only failing requirement is runtime (10 items with placeholder values).

**How cleaning changed the numbers (August 2026, company-wide).** This page is a fixed snapshot for the reporting month and isn't affected by filters on other pages. Each headline metric was computed twice with the same definition: once straight from the raw tables and once from the clean layer. Impact level: High = 20%+ difference, Medium = 5–20%, Low = under 5% (a judgment call). Issue numbers refer to issue\_log.md in the repo.

title.value: Impact of cleaning on headline metrics
MRR from raw to clean (Aug 31, 2026)

description.value: Raw MRR is $9,245.77; clean MRR is $3,956.01. Placeholder prices of $999.99 (step 4) explain 90% of the gap. The step order is a choice; a different order splits the amounts slightly differently, but the total is the same.

title.value: Rows kept, flagged and quarantined by table

description.value: Every raw row ends up in exactly one place: the clean layer (kept, possibly flagged) or quarantine (excluded, with a reason). Counts cover each whole table, not one month.

title.value: Quarantine and flag reasons

description.value: Why rows were quarantined or flagged, by table. Quarantined rows are excluded from all metrics; flagged rows are kept and can be filtered.
